guide.content:
# Planning Center usage

Purpose: Grace Church staff operations

Reachable products: People, Services, Groups, Check-Ins, Calendar, Registrations, Giving, Publishing, Webhooks.

API pins: people 2026-06-04, services 2018-11-01, groups 2023-07-10, check-ins 2025-05-28, calendar 2026-06-22, registrations 2025-05-01, giving 2019-10-18, publishing 2024-03-25, webhooks 2022-10-20, api 2026-09-24.

Stored credentials and private calendar access codes are permanently withheld.

## Identity first

A People person id joins records across products. Resolve people by identity,
then join on `person_id`; names can repeat. A membership, scheduled person,
workflow card and person each have their own record id.

`get_me` identifies the token's user and the organization's time zone. Bare
dates mean the organization's local day; use a timestamp with an offset for
an exact boundary. Name filters are exact unless their value ends in `%`.

An old person id may have been merged. Read `/people/v2/person_mergers` with
`where[person_to_remove_id]`, follow `person_to_keep_id`, then read that profile.
An empty history does not establish that a person was merged.

Reduce pastoral information inside `execute_code` and return aggregates unless
the task needs named people. A named projection omits some safe vendor fields;
read the indexed record when the task needs those fields.

## People and follow-up

Resolve a person before changing their profile. An omitted attribute leaves
the current value alone; `null` clears it. Archiving a person is reversible;
deleting a profile is permanent.

Workflow cards join people to a workflow and its ordered steps. Resolve both
the card id and its person id before acting on a card. Snoozing needs a duration;
promoting a card completes its step, while skipping moves on without completing
it. A workflow card note and a profile note are different records. Profile note
categories can notify their subscribers.

Custom field values need their field-definition records to supply names and
data types. Form answers similarly join submissions, values and fields; the
API cannot submit a form on someone's behalf.

Saved People lists are live cross-product queries. Their results are only as
fresh as their last refresh. Refreshing a list can fire its automations, such
as adding a person to a workflow, and is a write even when the task is a count.

## Services plans and schedules

Resolve the service type before finding a dated plan. Plan times define the
service dates. `get_plan` combines the plan, order of service and scheduled
team; a cut section can be read through its indexed items or team-members path.
Item durations are seconds, so divide by 60 when reporting minutes.

Scheduling needs a team and may need a position. `C` means confirmed, `U`
unconfirmed and `D` declined. Preparing a notification and sending it are
different actions. A song item's identity comes from its song and arrangement;
musical keys are not credentials. Services cannot upload a file through this
connection.

## Groups membership joins

Use a group's membership records to distinguish leaders from members. On this
API version memberships carry no person attributes; `include=person` supplies
names, and the related person id supplies contact details and other product
records. The API can change memberships and group settings, but cannot create
a group, create a meeting or record group attendance.

## Check-Ins occurrences

An event is recurring; its event period is a dated occurrence. Period counts
are the efficient attendance answer. Individual check-ins join a person to a
period, and date filtering uses the period's start, not the check-in's creation
time. The API cannot check anyone in or out.

## Calendar occurrences

Event instances expand recurrence into occurrences. A booking can return a
`BookedEvent` stub when the user lacks access to its event. Events, instances
and times are read-only; tags, resources, rooms and folders have write APIs.

## Registrations

A signup describes a registration event. Its attendee records join back to
People and distinguish active, waitlisted and canceled attendees. This API
cannot register someone.

## Giving amounts and donor joins

Amounts are integer cents with an explicit currency. A donation's designations
allocate it across funds; do not count a donation once per designation. Join
donors by person id and funds by fund id. Recurring schedules and the donations
they produce are different records. Creating/editing a donation, refunding it
or committing a batch changes financial records; named giving tools only read.

## Publishing

Episodes, channels and resources are available through the indexed API. A public
Church Center link and a media resource are different things; use the record
the task asks for.

## Webhooks

A subscription names an event and callback destination. Signing keys, private
download destinations and opaque event/delivery payloads or headers remain
withheld. Status and event metadata are available for audits.

## Organization API

The organization API includes application metadata and personal-access-token
inventory. Inventory records describe tokens; they do not return their values.
Revoking a token is a write and may interrupt another integration.

## Not available

Only reviewed product versions and indexed operations are callable. File
uploads use a separate host this connection does not reach. Credentials and
private calendar access codes cannot be recovered through a tool.

## Conventions

- **Paging:** a paged `list_*` or `search_*` read takes `limit` (default 25, at most 100) and `cursor`. While `page.hasMore` is true, pass `page.nextCursor` back unchanged as `cursor`; the last page has no `nextCursor`.
- **Results:** `fields` narrows a read's result to the dot paths you name. `truncated` lists the dot paths a result cut for size; the ids that fetch what was cut stay in the result.
- **Hatch:** `pco_api_search` finds this API's operations and reads no account data, `pco_api_details` shows one operation's contract, and `pco_api_read` calls a reviewed read. `pco_api_write` calls a reviewed write, and every call to it needs approval. An operation without a reviewed verdict is refused; these are refused by design: `POST /people/v2`.
- **Writes:** a write is sent once and never retried. When its outcome is unknown, read the target before repeating it. Writes take no idempotency key.
- **Errors:** codes come from the vendor's statuses and error facts, never its prose. `not_found` means the record does not exist; this API tells absence from a permission gap. `conflict` means: HTTP 409 for duplicate records in People.
- **Withheld values:** a value withheld for safety reads `"[redacted]"`. Writes refuse whole marker values and withheld links; longer prose may mention the marker. Paths and queries refuse any containment.

tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Get the Planning Center person this token acts as, with the organization's name and time zone. Supplies personId for my-schedule and assignee questions.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: search_people
tools.description: Search People profiles by name, email, or phone, with each person's primary email and phone. Omit search to list everyone; never searches custom fields or notes.

search.description: Matches name, email address, or phone number.

updatedSince.description: Only people updated at or after this time. ISO 8601 date or date-time; a bare date is the organization's local day.

order.description: Sort attribute; a leading '-' reverses it.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: get_person
tools.description: Get one person's profile with every email, phone number, address, household, and primary campus. Custom fields are list_person_field_data.

personId.description: Person id from search_people. The same id resolves in every Planning Center product.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: create_person
tools.description: Create a People profile. Emails and phone numbers are separate records; add them after with add_person_email and add_person_phone_number.

gender.description: Gender as the organization records it, e.g. Male or Female.

membership.description: Membership type, one of the organization's own values such as Member or Visitor.

child.description: Whether the person is a child.

tools.name: update_person
tools.description: Update fields on one People profile; omitted fields stay as they are. status inactive archives the person reversibly; this never deletes a profile.

personId.description: Person id from search_people. The same id resolves in every Planning Center product.

gender.description: Gender as the organization records it, e.g. Male or Female.

membership.description: Membership type, one of the organization's own values such as Member or Visitor.

child.description: Whether the person is a child.

status.description: inactive archives the profile; active restores it.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: List People workflows with their steps and ready, overdue, and unassigned card counts. Archived workflows are excluded unless asked for.

name.description: Exact workflow name; end it with % for a prefix match.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: list_workflow_cards
tools.description: List the cards in one workflow with each card's person, assignee, and current step. Card actions need both the card id and its person_id.

stage.description: Card stage as Planning Center reports it, e.g. ready, snoozed, completed, removed.

stepId.description: Only cards on this step (list_workflows steps[].id).

assigneeId.description: Only cards assigned to this person id.

order.description: Sort attribute; a leading '-' reverses it.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: add_workflow_card
tools.description: Add a person to a workflow as a new card on its first step. Optionally assign it; the workflow's own step defaults apply otherwise.

personId.description: Person id from search_people. The same id resolves in every Planning Center product.

assigneeId.description: Person id to assign the card to.

tools.name: apply_workflow_card_action
tools.description: Promote, send back, skip a step on, snooze, unsnooze, remove, or restore one workflow card. Never emails; sending a card email is pco_api_write.

action.description: promote completes the step; skip_step moves on without completing it; go_back returns to the previous step.

snoozeDays.description: Days to snooze; required with action snooze and refused otherwise.

tools.name: list_person_notes
tools.description: List the notes on one person's profile with their category names, newest first by default. Workflow card notes are not profile notes.

personId.description: Person id from search_people. The same id resolves in every Planning Center product.

order.description: Sort attribute; a leading '-' reverses it.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: add_person_note
tools.description: Add a note to a person's profile in a note category. Category subscribers may be notified; read categories at /people/v2/note_categories.

personId.description: Person id from search_people. The same id resolves in every Planning Center product.

noteCategoryId.description: Note category id; Planning Center files every note under one.

tools.name: list_person_field_data
tools.description: List one person's custom field values, each labeled with its field name and data type. Writing a value is pco_api_write at /people/v2/field_data.

personId.description: Person id from search_people. The same id resolves in every Planning Center product.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: list_service_types
tools.description: List Services service types — the recurring services such as Sunday Morning. Supplies serviceTypeId for plans and teams.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.description: List one service type's plans (individual services) by date. Defaults to upcoming plans, soonest first; get_plan returns the order of service and team.

when.description: future (default) sorts soonest first; past sorts most recent first.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: Get one plan with its times, order of service, and scheduled team in a single call. Reports truncated sections past 100 rows; the hatch pages the remaining items and team.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in the result, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: list_teams
tools.description: List one service type's teams with their positions. Supplies teamId and position names for schedule_plan_person.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: list_person_schedules
tools.description: List where one person is scheduled to serve across every service type, with team, position, and response. Defaults to upcoming.

personId.description: Person id from search_people. The same id resolves in every Planning Center product.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: schedule_plan_person
tools.description: Schedule a person on a plan's team, unconfirmed by default. Prepares a notification only when asked; Planning Center sends it, not this call.

personId.description: Person id from search_people. The same id resolves in every Planning Center product.

prepareNotification.description: Queue Planning Center's scheduling notification for this person.

tools.name: list_groups
tools.description: List Groups groups with type, schedule, and member count. Archived groups are excluded unless asked for; the API cannot create a group.

name.description: Exact group name; end it with % for a prefix match.

archived.description: Archived groups: exclude (default), include, or only.

order.description: Sort attribute; a leading '-' reverses it.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: list_group_memberships
tools.description: List one group's members and leaders with their names and join dates. Contact details come from get_person with person_id.

order.description: Sort attribute; a leading '-' reverses it.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: add_group_member
tools.description: Add a person to a group as a member or leader. Fails when they already belong; change a role or remove someone with pco_api_write.

personId.description: Person id from search_people. The same id resolves in every Planning Center product.

joinedAt.description: When they joined. Defaults to now. ISO 8601 date or date-time; a bare date is the organization's local day.

tools.name: list_donations
tools.description: List Giving donations with their fund designations, newest first, by date, fund, or donor. Amounts are integer cents. Read-only.

receivedAfter.description: Only donations received at or after this time. ISO 8601 date or date-time; a bare date is the organization's local day.

receivedBefore.description: Only donations received before this time. ISO 8601 date or date-time; a bare date is the organization's local day.

fundId.description: Only donations designated to this fund (list_funds).

succeededOnly.description: Exclude pending and failed card or ACH payments.

order.description: Sort attribute; a leading '-' reverses it.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: list_funds
tools.description: List Giving funds with ledger codes and visibility. Supplies fundId for donation filters.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in each item, e.g. ["id"]. It only narrows the result.

tools.name: pco_api_search
tools.description: Find Planning Center API operations by keyword or path. Returns up to 8 compact matches with the tool that calls each; reads no account data.

query.description: Keywords or a path, e.g. refund charge.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous search with the same query.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

matched.description: The request or response field this operation was found by; call its tool to read the field.

truncated.description: Entry labels cut for size; pco_api_details on that method and path returns them whole.

tools.name: pco_api_details
tools.description: Read one Planning Center API operation's request contract: path, query and body parameters with types and required names. Reads no account data.

path.description: The path template from search, or a concrete path.

param.description: Return only this parameter, in full.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous details call with the same method, path and param.

body.description: Body content type and schema. When paged: this page's properties, the required names it delivers or chunks, and the schema's other keywords on the page that carries them.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

of.description: The piece this text belongs to, such as parameters.limit.

text.description: Part of that piece's JSON; join the parts in page order, then parse them.

truncated.description: Labels cut for size; their full text arrives as chunks.

page.description: Present when the contract exceeds one answer: pass nextCursor back for the next pieces.

tools.name: pco_api_read
tools.description: Call a reviewed Planning Center API read. The operation index checks arguments before anything is sent. JSON:API records retain data, included and meta; named reads resolve common joins.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /people/v2/people/123. No query string.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.

param.description: Put nextCursor in this vendor parameter, unchanged.

tools.name: pco_api_write
tools.description: Call a reviewed Planning Center API write; method and path are stated for approval, and the operation index checks arguments first. Bodies are JSON:API documents, not flat attributes.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /people/v2/people/123. No query string.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

body.description: Request body as JSON fields, named as details lists them; form operations are encoded for you.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.
